description: Median imputation helper used by compute_complexity_score: a feature absent from appdetails (or not yet normalizable, e.g. pre-freeze complexity_bounds) contributes its weight at the cohort median rather than at zero, and the row records which features were imputed (FORMULATION.md section 4, 'Missing values' note).
docstring:
Impute NaN entries at the column's own median and flag which rows were imputed.

Args:
    values: A single already-normalized-to-[0,1] feature column (post normalize_feature_log_scaled / compute_tag_score / linear normalization) for the candidate cohort, with NaN for rows where the raw input was missing or the feature was not yet normalizable.

Returns:
    (imputed_values, was_imputed): imputed_values has every NaN replaced by nanmedian(values) computed over the non-NaN entries of THIS SAME candidate cohort (i.e. 'the cohort median' is always run-local, never a cross-run or hard-coded constant); was_imputed is a boolean Series, True exactly where an original NaN was replaced.

Raises:
    ValueError: If values is entirely NaN (no cohort median exists to impute from) -- compute_complexity_score must catch this per-feature case and treat that feature's weight as contributing 0.5 (the normalized-scale midpoint) as a documented last-resort fallback, since a feature missing for 100% of a run's candidates cannot be median-imputed from that run's own data.
preconditions: values is a 1-D numeric Series already scaled to [0,1] (or at least a consistent unit) before this call -- imputation happens post-normalization, per FORMULATION.md's phrasing 'contributes its weight at the cohort median', which is a statement about the normalized feature, not the raw input
postconditions: was_imputed is True at exactly the positions where values was NaN
Non-NaN entries of values are returned completely unchanged in imputed_values

edge_cases.expected_behavior: imputed_values equals values exactly; was_imputed is all False
raises ValueError; caller (compute_complexity_score) applies the documented 0.5-fallback and must itself flag this as an unusually severe missing-data condition worth a run-level warning event

edge_cases.input: values with an even number of non-NaN entries (median falls between two values)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: standard pandas/numpy median interpolation (average of the two middle values) is used, no special-casing

unit_tests.name: test_no_missing_values_unchanged
unit_tests.description: A Series with no NaN returns itself unchanged and was_imputed all False.

unit_tests.name: test_imputes_at_median_and_flags
unit_tests.description: A Series [0.2, NaN, 0.4, 0.6] imputes the NaN at median(0.2,0.4,0.6)=0.4 and flags position 1.
